title: The Room of Cold Spring
premise: Felix Thackeray, a property surveyor who has spent twelve years living quietly in the house she was hired to appraise, discovers that her sleep recordings capture a second voice answering questions she doesn't remember asking. The house is a chorus of everyone who stayed too long, and it wants a new verse added to its song. As Felix uncovers the fates of the previous occupants, she realizes the only escape is to learn the song's final verse without ever singing it aloud, because the moment she harmonizes, she belongs to the room forever. In the end, Felix chooses truth over belonging, singing the verse wrong on purpose, and walks out at dawn while the house, unfinished, begins calling her name in her own voice.
about_author: Mara Okafor is a former building inspector who spent a decade documenting condemned properties across the American Midwest. She writes horror rooted in the uncanny intimacy of houses, drawing on the paperwork, silences, and small wrongnesses she catalogued in her inspection years.

chapters.title: The Appraisal That Never Closed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Twelve years after arriving to appraise 14 Cold Spring Lane, Felix still lives there, keeping the survey unfinished and herself invisible. She catalogs the house's small wrongnesses: doors ajar, measurements that shift, a hum in the walls at 3 a.m. Emotional beat: brittle denial, the comfort of routines that keep the truth at arm's length.

chapters.title: White Noise, Second Voice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A neighbor's gift of a sleep recorder captures Felix asking questions in her sleep and a low, patient voice answering. The voice knows her childhood address. She tells herself it's a radio bleed-through, but replays the tape until dawn. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession; the first crack in her twelve-year denial.

chapters.title: The Previous Owners' File
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Digging through county records, Felix finds the house has had seven owners in forty years, each deed transferred by 'estate of' though no one died in the records. She visits the last owner's sister, who begs Felix to leave and mentions a song their mother hummed at the end. Emotional beat: the past pressing in; loyalty to her own secrecy versus the pull of truth.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with recorded transcripts interleaved. The voice begins asking Felix questions while she's awake: what she abandoned, who she left behind, what she traded for quiet. She answers one, honestly, and every door in the house opens at once. Emotional beat: vertigo of being known; the intoxicating horror of finally being addressed.

chapters.title: What the Walls Keep
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Behind the upstairs wallpaper Felix finds names scratched in layers, each ending mid-word. The hum resolves into melody, and she recognizes it: a lullaby her own mother sang, a song she's never told anyone. The house isn't random; it collects what you hide. Emotional beat: violation and grief; the realization that invisibility was never protection.

chapters.title: The Sister's Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the sister, Ruth, in a care home, recounting her brother's last weeks, when he sang the lullaby's final verse and stopped speaking entirely, smiling, waiting. Ruth gives Felix a torn hymnal page with the verse, half-burned. Emotional beat: pity and terror; the price of survival made concrete in another survivor's ruin.

chapters.title: Harmonizing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The house stops pretending. Rooms rearrange to trap her; the voice sings the lullaby and Felix's throat moves without her permission, one note escaping before she bites it down. The house rewards her with warmth, belonging, a vision of everyone who stayed, content. Emotional beat: temptation at its sweetest; loyalty to the self versus the seduction of joining something.

chapters.title: The Last Verse, Half-Learned
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She studies the burned page, reconstructing the final verse: it's a renunciation, a song that must be sung wrong to be refused. The voice pleads, then threatens, wearing her mother's tone now. Felix rehearses silently, mouthing the words, learning the melody only to break it. Emotional beat: grim resolve; preparation as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Night the House Sings Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The house takes her voice entirely and sings the lullaby in her register, filling the room with her own harmonies, trying to complete the song for her. In the climax, Felix screams the final verse deliberately off-key, wrong notes, broken rhythm, a refusal made of sound. The house shudders; the walls bleed cold spring water; the chorus goes silent mid-verse. Emotional beat: agonizing release; truth wielded as a weapon against belonging.

chapters.title: Vacant, As Of
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, coda. At dawn Felix signs the appraisal she never finished, marks the property 'vacant, as of,' and walks out with the recorder still running. Behind her the house hums the lullaby in her own voice, calling her name, unfinished, patient. She doesn't look back, but the last line of the recording is her sleeping voice, that night, humming the first bar. Emotional beat: survival with a scar; the price paid, and the question of what she carried out.
